prompt: Luis is a registered agent of a broker-dealer. On weekends he is paid by an unrelated state-registered adviser to introduce neighbors and explain that adviser's wrap program. He places no trades for the adviser. What does the Uniform Securities Act require for the weekend work?

options.text: His current agent registration is enough, because introducing neighbors is treated as selling securities for the broker-dealer
He must register as an IAR of that adviser
He must register an investment adviser in his own name, because weekend referrals are a separate advisory firm
He needs no registration at all, because he names no security and only describes the wrap program

explanation: Soliciting or offering advisory services for compensation makes Luis an investment adviser representative under the Uniform Securities Act. His agent registration authorizes securities transactions for the broker-dealer. It does not authorize weekend introductions for an adviser, so he must register as that adviser's IAR. Describing the wrap program is still a solicitation of advisory services.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats an agent license as covering advisory solicitation; selling securities for a broker-dealer and soliciting an adviser's clients are different registrations.
distractorExplanations.c: Makes him the adviser rather than its representative; he solicits for the existing firm and does not open an advisory business of his own.
distractorExplanations.d: Stops at the missing stock pick; the Act covers soliciting advisory services even when the solicitor names no particular security.

prompt: Helen works for an SEC-registered adviser whose headquarters is in another state. She lists her house in this state on the firm website and meets clients there each month. Her only clients are 8 natural persons, and none of them is a qualified client. Where must Helen register?

options.text: In no state, because advising 8 natural persons fits a de minimis exclusion for representatives of federal covered advisers
Only with the SEC, together with the advisory firm that already holds federal registration
With this state's Administrator
As an agent of a broker-dealer in this state, because a house used for meetings functions as a sales branch

explanation: A supervised person of a federal covered adviser must register as an investment adviser representative in a state where she has a place of business if she has more than five natural-person clients, other than qualified clients, and those clients are more than 10 percent of her clients. Helen's house is named on the firm website and used for monthly meetings, so it is her place of business in this state. Her only clients are 8 natural persons and none of them is a qualified client, so both parts of that client test are met. Advising those 8 clients is not a de minimis exclusion. The SEC registers the firm, not Helen.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats those 8 natural persons as a de minimis exclusion; none is a qualified client, the count is more than five, and she meets them at a place of business in this state.
distractorExplanations.b: Sends the representative to the SEC; the Commission registers the advisory firm and does not register its individual representatives.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses her with an agent of a broker-dealer; advisory meetings at the listed house are an IAR place of business, not a brokerage sales office.

prompt: Noah, registered with a broker-dealer, fills customer orders and is paid only commissions. If a customer has already chosen the security, Noah explains the order type and charges no separate advice fee. Under the Uniform Securities Act, which registration does that work require?

options.text: Investment adviser representative registration, because explaining an order is advice paid for by the commission
Agent registration plus investment adviser representative registration, because any remark about a security creates a second license
No registration of either kind, because the Act does not treat a commission as compensation
Registration only as an agent of his broker-dealer

explanation: An agent represents a broker-dealer in effecting securities transactions. Comments that are solely incidental to that brokerage, with no separate advisory fee, do not make Noah an investment adviser representative. The commission pays for the trade the customer already chose, so the Uniform Securities Act requires his agent registration and not an IAR registration.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats an incidental order explanation as advisory business; without a separate fee, that comment stays inside the agent role.
distractorExplanations.b: Collapses the two licenses; a remark about a trade the customer already chose does not automatically create investment adviser representative status.
distractorExplanations.c: Misreads the commission as if it erased registration; that pay is brokerage compensation, which is why the agent registration applies.

prompt: A state-registered adviser gives Andre discretion to rebalance client portfolios to a written model. He never calls clients and never solicits. Relationship managers handle every conversation. Under the Uniform Securities Act, what is Andre?

options.text: An IAR, because managing the accounts is enough
An agent of a broker-dealer, because a rebalancing trade can be done only by an agent and never by an IAR
Clerical staff with no registration, because he never speaks to clients and only applies a model someone else wrote
A brokerage research analyst, whose FINRA license stands in for state investment adviser representative registration

explanation: Managing client accounts or portfolios is an investment adviser representative function under the Uniform Securities Act, with or without client conversations. Andre's discretion to rebalance the accounts is that function, so he registers as an IAR. The relationship managers do not take the duty off the person who manages the portfolios, and a brokerage license does not replace the state registration.

distractorExplanations.b: Confuses an IAR with an agent of a broker-dealer; managing advisory accounts is not the same as representing a broker-dealer in customer trades.
distractorExplanations.c: Misuses the clerical exclusion; discretion to rebalance client accounts is portfolio management, not ministerial paperwork.
distractorExplanations.d: Substitutes a FINRA license for the state registration; NASAA's Act still requires an IAR registration when the person manages accounts.

prompt: A yoga-studio owner holds no securities license. A state-registered adviser pays her a flat fee whenever a member signs the adviser's contract. She hands over the brochure and never names a security. Under the Uniform Securities Act, what is she?

options.text: An agent of a broker-dealer, because the flat fee pays her for a securities transaction
A solicitor who must register as an IAR
Outside the Act, because handing out a brochure without naming a security is not advisory activity
An investment adviser in her own name, because the flat fee means she no longer acts for the other adviser

explanation: The Uniform Securities Act includes, as an investment adviser representative, a person who solicits or offers an adviser's services. The studio owner is paid to bring in advisory clients, so she must register as an IAR even though she never names a security. She is not effecting trades for a broker-dealer, and the fee does not make her a separate advisory firm.

distractorExplanations.a: Confuses a solicitor with an agent of a broker-dealer; she is not effecting purchases or sales of securities for a broker-dealer.
distractorExplanations.c: Ignores the solicitation clause; passing the brochure for a fee is offering advisory services, which the Act covers without a security name.
distractorExplanations.d: Treats the solicitor as the adviser; she acts for the state-registered firm, so she registers as its representative.

prompt: Northbridge is a federal covered adviser and has already notice-filed in this state. It then leases a room and assigns Priya to meet clients there 3 days each week. What must Priya do before she advises from that room?

options.text: Rely on the notice filing, which already registers every individual who will work from the new room
Register with the SEC, because representatives of a federal covered adviser are not registered by any state
Register as an IAR with this state's Administrator
Register as an agent of a broker-dealer, because a leased room used on a weekly schedule is a retail sales office

prompt: A state Administrator is reviewing four people who give investment-related advice. Which one meets the definition of an investment adviser under the Uniform Securities Act?

A broker-dealer that gives advice incidental to trades for no fee beyond commissions

distractorExplanations.c: Overstates preemption. The state cannot require registration, but it may require a notice filing and a fee, and it keeps antifraud authority.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses an investment adviser with a broker-dealer. Serving advisory clients in a new state does not make the firm a broker-dealer.

prompt: While drafting a will, a lawyer tells the client that municipal bonds the client already owns can be placed in a testamentary trust. She charges her ordinary legal fee and does not advertise investment advice. How does the Uniform Securities Act classify her?

options.text: As an investment adviser, because she named a type of security while performing legal work for a client
As a federal covered adviser, because a lawyer who mentions securities in a will is regulated by the SEC instead of the state
As excluded, because the securities comment is solely incidental to her law practice
As an investment adviser, because she collected a legal fee for a meeting in which a security was discussed

explanation: The Uniform Securities Act excludes a lawyer whose investment advice is solely incidental to the practice of law. A comment about bonds the client already owns, made while drafting a will, billed as a legal fee, and without an offer of advisory services, stays inside that exclusion. Naming a security during legal work does not create an advisory business, and it does not make the lawyer a federal covered adviser.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats a mention of a security as an advisory business. A comment that is solely incidental to legal work stays inside the lawyer exclusion.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the lawyer exclusion with federal coverage. Mentioning bonds in estate documents does not make the lawyer an adviser registered with the SEC.
distractorExplanations.d: Misreads compensation. The ordinary legal fee does not end the exclusion when the advice remains solely incidental to the practice of law.

prompt: The Harbor Gazette, a newspaper of general and regular circulation, runs a weekly column of impersonal market commentary addressed to its readers as a group. The column is not written for any one subscriber. Under the Uniform Securities Act, what is the publisher?

options.text: An investment adviser, because subscribers pay for a newspaper that comments on whether markets look attractive
A federal covered adviser that must notice-file in each state where copies of the paper are sold
An investment adviser in the state with the highest circulation and excluded from the definition in the other states
Excluded, as the publisher of a bona fide newspaper of general and regular circulation

explanation: The Act excludes the publisher of a bona fide newspaper, news magazine, or business or financial publication of general and regular circulation. Impersonal market commentary sent to readers as a group fits that exclusion. The price of the paper is not an advisory fee, selling copies does not make the publisher a federal covered adviser, and the exclusion is not limited to the state where the most copies are sold.

distractorExplanations.a: Treats the newspaper's price as an advisory fee. A bona fide paper of general and regular circulation is excluded even though readers pay for it.
distractorExplanations.b: Confuses the publisher exclusion with federal coverage. An impersonal newspaper column does not make the publisher an adviser registered with the SEC.
distractorExplanations.c: Splits the exclusion by sales. The newspaper exclusion does not depend on which state sells the most copies.

prompt: Helen is paid to tell clients whether to buy rare coins and rental houses. She does not mention stocks, bonds, funds, or any other security. Under the Uniform Securities Act, which statement is correct?

options.text: She is not an investment adviser, because the advice does not concern securities
She is an investment adviser, because paid guidance about where to put money meets the definition without a security
She is an investment adviser when the coins or houses are bought in a retirement account, even if she names no security
She is a federal covered adviser, because recommendations of coins and rental real estate are overseen by the SEC

explanation: The investment adviser definition applies to advice about securities given for compensation as a business. Rare coins and rental houses are not securities, so Helen's recommendations do not enter the definition. Buying those assets inside a retirement account does not turn them into securities. Federal covered adviser status is for an adviser registered with the SEC, not for a person who recommends coins and real estate.

distractorExplanations.b: Drops the securities requirement. Paid advice about coins and houses is not advice about securities, so the investment adviser definition is not met.
distractorExplanations.c: Invents a retirement-account test. The coins and houses are still not securities, and the type of account does not create an investment adviser.
distractorExplanations.d: Confuses non-securities with federal coverage. Coins and real estate are not securities, and a federal covered adviser is an adviser registered with the SEC.

prompt: Elm Street Advisory is not a federal covered adviser. It keeps its only office in State K and advises residents of that state from the office. Under the Uniform Securities Act, what must the firm do to advise those clients lawfully?

options.text: Register with the SEC rather than State K, because an office in one state makes the firm federal covered
Use the de minimis exemption in State K, because its clients live in the state where the office is located
Register as an investment adviser in State K, where it has its place of business
Register in the states that border State K, because an office there creates a registration duty in each neighboring state

explanation: An adviser that is not federal covered must register with the state in which it maintains a place of business. Elm Street's office in State K, used to advise that state's residents, is a place of business, so State K registration is required. An office in one state does not make the firm federal covered. The de minimis exemption does not apply in a state where the adviser has an office, and neighboring states are not added when the firm has neither an office nor clients there.

distractorExplanations.a: Invents a path to federal coverage. Keeping an office in one state does not make the firm a federal covered adviser or remove the duty to register in that state.
distractorExplanations.b: Misapplies the de minimis exemption. That exemption is for an adviser with no place of business in the state, and this firm has its office in State K.
distractorExplanations.d: Invents a neighboring-state duty. Registration follows the firm's place of business and its clients, and the stem gives the firm neither an office nor clients outside State K.
